sources.claim: Evaluate task outcomes with appropriate graders and inspect agent execution; repeated trials measure reliability.
Benchmark contamination and faulty tests can invalidate apparent coding performance; audit tasks and graders.
Routing is evaluated as a quality-cost tradeoff rather than agreement with a single preferred model label.
d1 supports typed Choice, Score and Noul decisions; its guide calls for evaluation of decision behavior on the user's task.

opinions.statement: For speed or cost guidance, first preserve acceptable correctness; a quick failed run is not a good recommendation.

For bounded code-only tasks, lower effort is a plausible starting candidate when comparable observed quality is adequate. Escalate effort when evidence supports improved correctness; do not assume higher effort always wins.
One success or a small decision-score difference is weak evidence. Treat close candidates as plausibly tied; reserve confidence for repeated, relevant, independently graded outcomes.
Code-only success cannot establish performance with filesystem, browser, network, or multi-file tools. Do not transfer this evidence to those harnesses without testing.

localEvidence.claim: Three configurations each passed one merge-intervals repair. This motivates a hypothesis, not a model ranking.

pricing.reason: Subscription usage does not provide per-task dollar prices. No price values are inferred from model names or token counts.

maintenance.pricingOrRetirementChange: invalidate affected price/availability records and rerun affected routing cases; do not retrain automatically
maintenance.newModel: discover actual harness support, add a separately budgeted candidate cohort, then test
maintenance.opinionChange: version the source and interpretation, run an ablation, and recheck the sealed held-out set only after selection
